newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanians in prayers protest against Israel fair.
newsitem.headline: Jordanians in prayers protest against Israel fair.

text.p: Some 2,500 Jordanians took part in Moslem Friday prayers in the street outside Amman's first Israeli trade fair to protest against the event.

Jordan deployed extra security and anti-riot police took up positions ahead of the prayers which also coincided with the start of the Moslem Holy month of Ramadan. Security forces formed a human chain to block worshippers gathered behind an intersection leading to the fair.

"Is this exhibition a reward for (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's intransigence?" Sheikh Hamza Mansour, a leading deputy spokesman of the Islamic Action Front (IAF), the kingdom's largest opposition party, told worshippers in a sermon.

The crowds of Jordanian women and men were heeding a call by a highly-publicised campaign led by a coalition of 21 parties, 18 unions and business lobbies against the Israeli trade fair, which opened last Wednesday.
Over 1,000 Jordanians ended their protest outside the fair on the first day of the exhibition in the largest anti-Israeli demonstration since Jordan's 1994 peace treaty.
The campaign reflects anti-Israeli feelings among many Jordanians who still shun contacts despite a 1994 peace treaty that ended a 46-year state of war with Israel.

Jordanians feel disappointed with Israel and support for normal ties has eroded since a right-wing Israeli government came to power last May on a platform that rejects swapping occupied Arab land for peace.
Seventy Israeli companies and over 200 Israeli businessmen are taking part in the fair that ends on Saturday.
